skill.name: github-cli
skill.description: Guides agents to use GitHub CLI for read-only context about pull requests, issues, reviews, branches, CI status, and GitHub URLs.
skill.summary: Use GitHub CLI to gather pull request, issue, review, branch, and CI context before GitHub-related work.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced command examples, and illustrative GitHub URLs. The skill is a GitHub CLI context reference with no prompt injection, obfuscation, secrets access, or unauthorized endpoint. Operational risk remains because agents may use authenticated GitHub CLI access, so read-only and privacy guardrails should be explicit.

remediation.issue: Read-only intent is implied but not explicit.
remediation.suggestion: State that the skill should gather context only and should not merge, comment, label, or modify GitHub resources without an explicit user request.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub CLI use can expose private repository context.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to limit private repository summaries to the current task and confirm before querying ambiguous or sensitive repositories.

content.value_statement: GitHub work often needs PR, issue, review, and CI context that local git cannot show. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use gh read commands for richer context.
actual_capabilities: Recognizes PR, issue, branch, review, CI, and GitHub URL requests as triggers for GitHub context gathering.
Provides GitHub CLI commands for pull request details, diffs, comments, reviews, checks, issues, branches, releases, and workflow runs.
Shows how to inspect GitHub URLs by extracting the owner, repository, and item number.
Combines local git history with GitHub conversation and status context.
Recommends structured GitHub CLI output when parsed fields are useful.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI to be installed and authenticated outside the skill.
Can only access repositories and organization data allowed by the current GitHub token.
Does not perform write actions such as merging, commenting, labeling, or release creation.
Does not configure GitHub Enterprise hosts or custom authentication flows.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Gather the PR description, diff, comments, reviews, and checks before recommending code changes.

use_cases.title: Triage an Issue
use_cases.description: Read issue details, comments, labels, and related context before assigning or planning work.

use_cases.title: Investigate CI Status
use_cases.description: Check workflow runs and PR checks before diagnosing build or test failures.

prompt_templates.title: View PR Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GitHub CLI context gathering for PR 123. Summarize the description, review comments, changed files, and CI status before suggesting next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use repository issue context to summarize issue 456, its comments, labels, and related open work. Identify the likely owner.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Branch Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced branch and PR readiness check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GitHub CLI and local git context to compare my current branch with the remote branch. Report linked PRs, checks, and review blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a GitHub URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the repository and item number from this GitHub URL. Use the appropriate GitHub CLI commands to summarize context, discussion, and status.

output_examples.input: Review PR 123 before I change the code.
output: Summary of the PR purpose and current state.
Review comments grouped by file and topic.
CI status, failing checks, and suggested next actions.

output_examples.output: A concise issue summary with latest comments, labels, assignee, related work, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Is my branch ready to merge?
output: Local branch commits that are not on the base branch.

best_practices: Use read-only GitHub CLI commands first, then decide whether more repository context is needed.
Confirm repository owner and name before querying a URL or ambiguous branch.
Summarize sensitive private repository details only when they are needed for the current task.
anti_patterns: Running state-changing GitHub commands without an explicit user request.
Assuming local git contains review comments, issue discussion, or CI status.
Sharing private repository context outside the user requested scope.

faq.question: Does this skill install GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: No. GitHub CLI must already be installed in the environment where the agent runs.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. Access depends on the active GitHub CLI authentication and token permissions.

faq.question: Can it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if the current GitHub token can access those repositories.

faq.question: Does it make changes to GitHub?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow is for context gathering and read-only inspection.

faq.question: Why use GitHub CLI instead of git?
faq.answer: Git shows local commits and branches. GitHub CLI can show PRs, issues, comments, reviews, and CI status.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflow guidance when shell access, network access, and GitHub CLI are available.
